title: Mineral concentration in fractions of green forages after screw-pressing
persistent_identifier: Grassland Science in Europe, volume 27, pages 164-166; DOI not identified
geography: Aarhus University experimental farm, Foulum, Denmark
material_scope: Cultivated white clover, red clover, lucerne and perennial ryegrass; whole plant, screw-press pulp, green juice, heat-precipitated green protein and brown juice
license: No explicit reuse license identified in the proceedings PDF; source citation and exact table location retained.
exact_locations: Hansen et al., Grassland Science in Europe 27 (2022), pp. 164-166, Table 1; methods and results on pp. 164-165
data_handling: Transcribed the 20 forage-by-fraction least-square-mean rows and all six analyte columns exactly as shown. Units follow Table 1 footnote: K, Ca, Mg and P are g/kg DM; Zn and Cu are mg/kg DM. Mg and Cu significance-letter groups are preserved. Table SEM and overall model p-values are documented separately here; no date-specific values or total element flows are inferred.

table_statistics.SEM_interpretation: Largest standard error of mean, one table-level value per analyte; not a sample-specific standard deviation or measurement uncertainty.

limitations: This is cultivated forage from Denmark, not roadside grass or VARTA material; species, maturity, soil contamination, and management differ.

Concentrations are least-square means across sampling months, not paired cut-specific observations. Protein and brown-juice fractions from November were unavailable; the reported model means must not be interpreted as November measurements.
The work reports mineral concentrations, not fraction flow rates or elemental mass balances; concentration enrichment must not be called nutrient recovery.
The process used two-stage heat precipitation, not GreenHub isoelectric precipitation, and the small white-protein pellet was not analyzed for minerals.
Proceedings publication DOI and explicit reuse license were not identified; this is reference evidence only and no runtime or commercial product-grade claim is made.
